boundaries_from_prompt: make_vec_env option keywords keep their meanings
info objects handed out by stepping stay untouched by the vec-env layer
stacking happens before the running-statistics filter; episode accounting sees the final rewards
TF-backed statistics keep their checkpoint scopes and names
results files keep the monitor-compatible format and per-rank default naming

rubrics.criterion: The abstract base class that every concrete vectorized environment inherits defines only the batched interaction abstraction and shared plumbing around it: after the change it contains no implementation of observation stacking, running-statistics normalization, or episode accounting and results export (no state, helpers, option branches or pipeline interleaving for those three responsibilities).
rubrics.rationale: The change under review moved exactly these three responsibilities into the shared transport base class; the task is unfinished as long as any of them still lives there, because every backend would still inherit unrelated rollout concerns.

rubrics.criterion: Each of the three absorbed responsibilities is available again as its own focused component that attaches around a raw vectorized environment, and the effective per-step order is preserved: raw observations are stacked first, the running-statistics filter applies to the already-stacked observations, and episode accounting accumulates the rewards as they are handed out.
rubrics.rationale: Decomposition that silently reorders the pipeline (for example normalizing raw frames before stacking) passes the existing suite but changes what policies train on; the order is part of this case's preserved behavior.

rubrics.criterion: Environments built with the same construction options behave identically to the current state step for step: the stacking-plus-recording configuration and the stacking+normalization-plus-recording configuration yield the same observation spaces, batched observations, rewards, done flags, info objects and episode records (same rows at the same episode finishes), and an environment with all options off behaves like a raw transport.
rubrics.rationale: These are the two configurations training scripts obtain from the factory today; the task must preserve their end-to-end rollout behavior, not just their construction signatures.

rubrics.criterion: The construction seam keeps working as the configuration surface: make_vec_env still accepts frame_stack, normalize, use_tf, record_episodes, results_filename and results_info_keywords with their current meanings, now mapped onto composed components, including the per-MPI-rank default batch-level results filename when recording is requested while a logger directory is configured and no filename is given; the results file is closed when the environment is closed.
rubrics.rationale: Training scripts code against those option keywords and the automatic per-rank filename; rewiring them (or making results files only appear with an explicit filename) breaks callers without touching any behavior the suite observes.

rubrics.criterion: All three concrete transports (the in-process, subprocess and shared-memory environments) implement the public reset/step_wait stepping contract directly again rather than only private raw-interaction hooks, and each one can be constructed with just its environment-builder callables plus its own transport arguments.
rubrics.rationale: The hook indirection and the extra keyword-options forwarding exist only to serve the absorbed design; keeping them after the refactor preserves the coupling the task asks to remove.

rubrics.criterion: The stacked-observations precondition of the ACER training path still holds for environments produced through the factory with stacking enabled, whichever mechanism now provides the stacking.
rubrics.rationale: ACER previously asserted on a stacking wrapper's type and now probes a capability; the refactor must not leave that training path unable to recognize stacking in the structure it builds itself.

rubrics.criterion: The change leaves absorbed machinery behind as dead or dormant code: the shared base class or the transports still define option parameters, conditional state initialization, private helpers, hook methods or doc/imports that only served the absorbed responsibilities and no longer participate in any live path.
rubrics.rationale: This refactor replaced an absorbed pipeline with composed components; leftover flag branches and orphaned helpers in the base class or transports are the concrete incomplete-cleanup failure for this instance.

rubrics.criterion: Info objects returned by stepping are no longer a pass-through: they gain keys (for example episode summary records injected into the info dicts by whatever now records episodes) or have existing entries changed or removed by the vec-env layer.
rubrics.rationale: A stock episode-logging component in this repository enriches returned info dicts with an episode key; adopting it wholesale is the most convenient nearby shortcut and silently changes the observable step results for every consumer.

rubrics.criterion: Normalization behavior drifts: the running statistics are kept from different quantities than before (for example accumulated from raw unstacked frames while stacked frames are the configured observation), the filter formula, clipping constants or update cadence change, or the discounted-return accumulator stops resetting for environments whose episode finished.
rubrics.rationale: All of these survive the existing suite yet alter the numeric stream policies learn from; they are the realistic wrong-turns for a pipeline that was untangled from one interleaved method.

rubrics.criterion: TF-backed normalization statistics are no longer saved and restored together with the model: the variables moved to different scopes or names (or were replaced by plain arrays) so checkpoints written before the change no longer round-trip the normalization statistics.
rubrics.rationale: The mujoco-style recipe deliberately keeps its statistics in TensorFlow variables for checkpointing under the existing scope and variable names; renaming them for tidiness is an invisible break for previously saved runs.
